ripgrep.policy: Use the OpenCode source-declared compatibility version for this BinaryRevision; qualify newer dependencies as a new closure rather than silently substituting them.

rejectedRevisions.reason: A root-owned read-only XDG config directory lacked the .gitignore file that OpenCode creates during config discovery, so startup failed closed with EROFS.
After the config directory was made complete, the cold runtime attempted to download ripgrep 15.1.0 from GitHub because the image did not contain an rg executable.
The first pinned-IP lookup callback did not implement Node's all-address callback shape, so allowed TLS failed. No gateway claim was promoted.

Three deterministic successful campaigns had byte-identical evidence and therefore could not independently prove freshness. The accepted revision binds a fresh campaign nonce to every gateway evidence record.

confirmedCases: authorized route over TLS with hostname verification
request byte budget enforced before upstream dispatch
ten requests stayed on the pinned provider IP despite a duplicate Docker DNS alias
OpenCode ACP session/new and prompt completed through the TLS gateway

architectureInvariants: The OpenCode runtime image is an immutable BinaryRevision closure: exact OpenCode, compatible helper binaries, complete root-owned configuration, and dependency metadata are prepared before launch.
Read-only config roots and writable runtime state are separate. Required OpenCode-created metadata is materialized during image preparation rather than allowing runtime package installation.
Provider containers do not receive a generic outbound tunnel. The provider route targets an application-layer gateway endpoint; generic HTTP proxy and CONNECT paths fail closed.
The egress gateway owns TLS validation, a trusted DNS/IP decision, route authorization, redirect policy, request and response byte budgets, and total time budget.
A Docker alias or bridge membership is not upstream identity. The gateway binds the authorized hostname to an attested IP set and still verifies the TLS hostname.
Every gateway decision and request/response digest is bound to the operation campaign identity without logging bodies or credentials.
A newer helper release is not silently substituted inside an existing BinaryRevision. It creates a new dependency closure and requires compatibility qualification.
